title: Stability without concealment

elements.text: COMET-XAI LITE
Stability without concealment
Proposal + executed preliminary pilot | Core question inspired by Krishna et al. and groupShapley [S03, S04]

When does grouping correlated inputs improve explanation stability
without hiding useful information?
THE PROBLEM

Similar predictions can
produce different
feature rankings after
retraining.
THE TRAP

Shorter lists and random
grouping can also
appear more stable.
OUR TEST

Compare matched
groups; measure
stability plus fidelity and
cancellation.
Credit benchmark • interpretable baseline • controlled comparisons • eight weeks
[Student name] | [Roll number] | B.Tech IT, DTU | Prof. Rahul Gupta

notes: Opening, about 60 seconds. My project asks whether grouping correlated inputs makes model explanations more reliable, or only makes them look more consistent. Imagine six monthly bill amounts: models can distribute importance among these related measurements differently after retraining. I want to distinguish a useful group summary from a summary that hides information. I narrowed the initial COMET proposal because temporal recourse, conformal margins and feature selection would require different evidence. The scope is now feasible in eight weeks on a laptop. The work completed is the proposal audit, literature review and a reproducible logistic-regression pilot; the full experiment is not complete. Name and roll-number fields are editable. Do not call this a finished paper or a new Shapley algorithm.

title: What the literature establishes — and what we will test

elements.text: COMET-XAI LITE
What the literature establishes — and what we will test
Sources: SHAP [S01]; disagreement [S03]; groupShapley [S04]; ITNAC 2025 [N03]; agreement 2026 [N04]
SHAP + dependence
Credit depends on model, background and explanation game.
Lundberg & Lee; Aas et al.

Disagreement +
aggregation
Agreement is a research problem; fusion already exists.
Krishna et al.; Bhatt et al.

Grouped
explanations
groupShapley and recent robustness work are close prior art.
Jullum et al.; Hendro et al. (2025)

Proposed gap: test stability beyond matched random grouping,
together with information loss and known-ground-truth fidelity.

notes: About 75 seconds. SHAP explains a specified model output using a defined coalition-value game. Krishna and colleagues show that different explanation methods can disagree. groupShapley already explains groups, so grouping is not my invention. I also found a 2025 ITNAC paper on feature grouping for robust SHAP and a 2026 paper on agreement and faithfulness-weighted consensus. Their full methods need to be compared before a novelty claim. Our proposed question is whether correlation grouping beats random partitions with the same group sizes, while preserving fidelity and internal information. We will use synthetic cases with a known explanation game and public credit data. The contribution is an empirical evaluation protocol and findings, not an assertion that combining existing tools creates a new theory. Primary links: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12228 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.01602 ; https://doi.org/10.1109/ITNAC66378.2025.11302604 .

title: Methodology and controlled evaluation

elements.text: COMET-XAI LITE
Methodology and controlled evaluation
Core method: train-only correlation grouping; coalition sums; size-matched controls. No temporal or causal recourse claim.
Split + preprocess
Fit only on training data
Retrain + explain
Same held-out people
Group + controls
Match group sizes exactly
Evaluate
Stability AND retained detail
MEASURE

RBO stability • matched-random difference
Cancellation • synthetic attribution error
AP / ROC-AUC / Brier • runtime
CONTROL

No grouping • same-size random groups
Known additive + interaction cases
Fixed model/output/background per
comparison
Minimum scope: synthetic data + UCI credit; logistic + one tree family. HELOC is conditional on verified access.

notes: About 90 seconds. We split data before fitting preprocessing or clusters. We retrain several models and explain the same held-out individuals. Each explanation is a vector of contributions in a stated output scale. We summarize either individual features or groups formed from training correlation. We compare the resulting stability to random groups with exactly the same number and sizes of groups. That controls a major shorter-list artefact. Next, we examine cancellation, synthetic exact group values and perturbation fidelity so a stable summary cannot simply hide opposing components. The initial model is logistic regression, where interventional logit contributions have an exact closed form. A small tree model and TreeSHAP are planned. The primary partition stays fixed across retraining; reclustering uncertainty is a separate analysis. We keep data, explainer and retraining randomness distinct. Removing model features, causal recourse and drift guarantees are outside the minimum project.

11 groups; matched group sizes

Limit: one split, logistic model only. No significance, causal recourse or publication claim.

notes: About 90 seconds. The official UCI dataset contains 30,000 rows. Our pilot used 24,000 training and 6,000 test rows; 500 held-out rows were explained for ten bootstrap logistic models. Correlation grouping produced eleven groups from nineteen inputs. Its ranking RBO was .924, compared with .863 for random partitions with the same sizes: an absolute difference of .061. This is not a 6.1 percent improvement in correctness, and it is not a significance claim. Predictive metrics were AP .489, ROC-AUC .713 and Brier .148. Nine mathematical/data-contract checks pass; a repeated run reproduces deterministic outputs. The main limitation is one split and one simple model, including numeric handling of repayment-status codes. The next steps are synthetic ground truth, fidelity/cancellation analysis, a tree model and additional splits/data. I would like approval for this narrowed scope and feedback on whether an empirical evaluation paper meets project requirements. Target a future ICAIF call or a suitable ECML PKDD workshop, with final venue dependent on results.

title: The concepts you need before the experiment

elements.text: BACKUP 01 • FIRST PRINCIPLES
The concepts you need before the experiment
DTU • [Student name] • [Roll number] • Prof. Rahul Gupta • 28 October 2026
MODEL

Inputs → learned function → default
probability. Testing asks whether
predictions generalize.
ATTRIBUTION

A contribution to a stated model output,
relative to a specified background.
STABILITY

Does the explanation change when the
model is retrained on resampled data?
FIDELITY

Does the explanation reflect the
specified model/game? Stability alone is
insufficient.

notes: Use this if asked to define terms. A feature is an input column, a label is the observed outcome, and a model is a learned mapping. Local attribution concerns one row; global attribution aggregates rows. Stability, fidelity and usefulness are distinct. The full study guide begins before these terms and includes examples.

title: The “corrected” manual still needs correction

elements.text: BACKUP 02 • DOCUMENT AUDIT
The “corrected” manual still needs correction
Detailed 36-point audit with printed PDF page numbers is in the Research Dossier.
• Lower correlation cutoff → more merging, not more groups.
• Coalition sums are not generally Owen / exact group values.
• Mean logit transformed by sigmoid is not mean probability.
• Margin code has an order-statistic error; alpha direction is reversed.
• Static credit data cannot validate temporal, actionable recourse.
• Agreement, monotonicity and lower VIF do not prove explanation quality.

notes: The manual contains many sensible corrections but is not fully reliable. Lowering rho merges more groups, not fewer. The proposed quantile code can select the wrong order statistic. Alpha=0 is not a no-margin setting. Mean probability is not sigmoid of mean logit. An additive model does not automatically imply the needed additive conditional attribution game. PFI need not always understate correlated features. Historical repayment data do not support feasible causal recourse. These are reasons for a narrower design, not reasons to discard all explainability research.

title: A linear attribution you can calculate by hand

elements.text: BACKUP 03 • EXACT BASELINE
A linear attribution you can calculate by hand
Illustrative arithmetic, not a measured applicant. Pilot uses the same identity on standardized logit inputs.
Score = 3x₁ + 2x₂ Reference = (1, 2) Input = (2, 5)
BASE SCORE
CONTRIBUTIONS
RECONSTRUCTION

Always state the explained output scale. The pilot explains log-odds, not
percentage points.

notes: For score=3*x1+2*x2, reference means 1 and 2 give base 7. At x=(2,5), the feature differences contribute 3 and 6. They sum to the nine-point score difference, and base plus contributions equals sixteen. In logistic regression this is the logit score, not probability. The actual pilot calculates the background mean after each model’s fitted preprocessor and checks this identity for all 500 audit cases. This verifies implementation of a stated attribution, not that the model is causally correct.

title: Stable summaries can conceal different things

elements.text: BACKUP 04 • INFORMATION LOSS
Stable summaries can conceal different things
Coalition sum versus grouped game: groupShapley [S04]. Worked numbers are illustrative.
CANCELLATION

Feature credits: +5 and −4.8
Net group contribution: 0.2
Unsigned internal mass: 9.8
A stable net can hide strong
components.
GROUPING CHANGES THE GAME

Three-player unanimity game:
ordinary A + B = 2/3
merged {A,B} group = 1/2
Coalition sum ≠ exact group value.

Retain group summaries AND feature drill-down; test interactions with a small
exact oracle.

notes: Two different issues are shown. Cancellation: +5 and minus 4.8 net to .2, while the unsigned total is 9.8. Net contribution is legitimate but can hide strong opposing components. Game semantics: in a three-player unanimity game every feature gets one third; summing A and B gives two thirds. Treat AB as one group and C as another, and each group gets one half. So the order of grouping and Shapley computation matters. We retain within-group drill-down and use exact small-game values as an oracle.

notes: For the final study, save stratified train/development/test IDs. Train-only transforms and clusters prevent leakage. The primary experiment freezes the correlation partition while retraining models. A separate reclustering analysis measures group discovery uncertainty. A separate explainer-repeat experiment measures sampling variance. Add a synthetic known-game oracle and one tree family. HELOC is conditional on obtaining a verified release and dictionary. The study can succeed as a negative-result evaluation if gains vanish under controls; do not keep expanding modules to force a positive result.

title: Evaluation must measure more than consistency

elements.text: BACKUP 07 • METRICS
Evaluation must measure more than consistency
DTU • [Student name] • [Roll number] • Prof. Rahul Gupta • 28 October 2026
Stability
RBO at p=.85; sensitivity at .7/.95; fixed audit individuals.
Controlled gain

Correlation-group stability minus size-matched random-group
stability.
Retained information

Cancellation, drill-down, exact synthetic error and masker
sensitivity.
Model + uncertainty
AP / AUC / Brier; paired effects; honest conditional uncertainty.

notes: RBO is the primary ranking stability measure. The main effect subtracts the mean of matched random partitions, but this is still a descriptive effect until replicated. Cancellation captures net-versus-unsigned attribution compression. Synthetic oracle error compares against a defined exact game, not assumed causal truth. AP, AUC and Brier validate the predictor; they do not validate explanations. Borrower confidence intervals with fixed models are conditional intervals, not a universal measure of model uncertainty. Report all denominators and failures.

title: What would falsify the project hypothesis?

elements.text: BACKUP 08 • NEGATIVE RESULTS
What would falsify the project hypothesis?
DTU • [Student name] • [Roll number] • Prof. Rahul Gupta • 28 October 2026
EVIDENCE AGAINST

Random groups perform equally well.
Information loss offsets stability.
Results disappear on new splits.
Closest prior art already answers the
question.
HONEST RESPONSE

Report the failure conditions.
Keep all runs and controls.
Revise claims and scope.
Do not invent expected results or tune
on test.
Research quality comes from a valid answer, not from forcing a positive outcome.

notes: A useful project must be able to fail its hypothesis. If matched random groups are just as stable, there is little evidence that correlation-specific grouping is the cause. If group summaries hide major opposing contributions or fail known-game fidelity checks, stability is insufficient. If benefit exists only in one model/split, generality is weak. If closest prior work already includes the proposed controls, novelty must be revised. These cases can support a careful replication or limitation study, but they do not guarantee publication.

notes: Read the closest sources rather than memorizing citation counts. SHAP defines the attribution framework; Krishna documents disagreement; groupShapley is the central grouping baseline; Chen and colleagues explain model-versus-data semantics. The 2025 feature-grouping robustness paper and 2026 consensus/agreement paper require closest-work comparison before claiming novelty. Do not claim to have reviewed their entire full text if only metadata or abstract was accessible. The research dossier includes more than thirty linked primary sources and distinguishes unresolved references.
